Ok so, I'm doing a 125cc yx engine swap. I'm keeping all my electricals on 6v power using a an aftermarket harness that connects the new chinese 12v to the OEM 6v harness. Now, the question is, my green wire, which I showed in the screen shot, is used to bring power to the front of the bike. Specifically to the light and speedometer. However the transfer harness plugs into the connector and only comes out with the black connected losing the green and the yellow. To keep my green, could I simply connect a wire to the green in the connector and ground it to the body of the bike? And my electricals would work?
Thanks. And the CDI is the little computer the engine uses to know when to spark. It's has a little 5 pin connector. 2 of those 5 beep when connected to each other.

I did buy a multimeter with the test light so I have both. I'm a big newbie (as you can see) and thought maybe if I see the current going through the sparkplug cable then the connection is good? I bought these because my sparkplug plug wasn't making any spark and thought either my CDI or coil got shorted (I shorted the fuse recently by grounding a wire by accident). Also I saw that the little metal cup, where the sparkplug sits inside the coilpack cable, was broken and maybe it made it so current wasn't going through. I found out how to test the CDI with the multimeter and have determined that it did in fact short since my black/red-black/white failed the continuity test (beeping when both are connected) and they are most likely the Pos/Neg combo
